summary.text: 手 is a pictograph of a hand. Early bronze forms show branching strokes interpreted as fingers above a lower part described as an arm or palm; the exact anatomy is unsettled. The earliest graph evidence identified here is from Western Zhou bronze materials, but those examples do not establish a dated first use meaning “hand.”

formation.text: Pictographic (象形): the graph depicts a hand as a whole. The bronze form is interpreted as having finger branches above and an arm or palm below. No separate sound component or internal component split is supported.

history.text: The curated bronze-style image represents a form catalogued for Western Zhou materials; the seal-style image represents a later seal-script tradition. Both are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs, and the images do not by themselves establish a direct sequence of graphic change.
The cited paleographic discussions report 手 absent from oracle-bone inscriptions and distinguish other hand-shaped graphs. The dossier does not establish an oracle-bone form of 手.

uncertainties.text: The sources differ on whether the bronze graph’s lower part represents an arm alone or includes the palm. Its exact anatomy remains an interpretation; no primary inscription image was visually examined in this research.

Bronze examples are identified from the Western Zhou onward, but no individual earliest inscription date or semantic context for those occurrences is verified. The early hand meaning rests on graphic interpretation and later lexicographic analysis.
The dossier does not establish the spoken-word history of 手 or verify proposed comparisons with Proto-Sino-Tibetan vocabulary, Burmese, or 收.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze materials (earliest graph evidence identified; semantic context unverified)
senses.text: The graph is interpreted as depicting a hand, and later lexicographic evidence supports this meaning. The bronze occurrences themselves lack verified semantic contexts, so they do not establish a securely dated earliest use with this meaning.
Shuowen glosses 手 as 拳 (“fist”). Its commentator explains hand and fist as mutually explanatory; this account does not establish that “fist” was the original meaning.
A dictionary records this use with a citation to 宋書, but the evidence here does not establish when it arose or how it developed from the hand sense.
A dictionary records this use with a citation to 漢書, without establishing its date or a semantic pathway from the bodily sense.
A dictionary records 手 as a verb meaning “hold,” with a citation to 公羊傳. Its chronological relation to the hand noun is not established here.

limitations.text: The bronze graph evidence does not supply semantic contexts, and the transmitted classical citations are not independently dated excavated attestations. The dossier does not establish chronological priority among the listed uses or transitions connecting them.

overview.text: 手 depicts a hand as a whole. Early bronze forms are interpreted as showing finger branches above an arm or palm, though the precise anatomy is unsettled.
